doc.title: Ralph Sutton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 22, 1995

title: Clubs after the card and Eddie Condon's in 1948
summary: He worked the Hickory House, Village Vanguard and Embers before joining Eddie Condon's in 1948.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah I think so, quite a bit now. So you had a reputation, at least you had on your resume that you played with Teagarden. Did that help you get your next engagement?

Well I worked like at the Hickory House and the Village Vanguard. This was after I got my union card. The Embers, they used to call it “The Numbers,” The Embers, and different spots before I went to work at Eddie Condon’s in Greenwich Village. That was in 1948.
Could you describe for our students who may be trying to put things in a historical perspective, what —
That too. Was it hysterical back then?
Oh we had a few laughs.
